about: The one style every Clockwork Spire painting is generated with (docs/art-direction.md). core goes on every prompt; each kind adds its framing. Never edit for one asset: change it here, for all, with a decision.
core: storybook steampunk picture book illustration, bold thick black ink outlines around every shape, flat cel shading with soft painterly texture, rich brass and copper, teal accents, warm amber lamplight glow, light from the upper left, high quality
negative: photo, photorealistic, 3d render, blurry, lowres, jpeg artifacts, extra limbs, deformed, bad anatomy, text, watermark, signature, logo, cropped, multiple characters, airbrushed, glossy 3d render, photorealistic metal, chrome reflections, thin faint lines, octane render

character.framing: full body, whole figure visible, limbs held clearly apart from the body, isolated on a plain flat light gray background, no scenery, a single figure, one pose only
character.negative: background scenery, frame, border, circle, vignette, cropped feet, floor shadow pool, character sheet, turnaround, model sheet, reference sheet, multiple views, multiple poses, props laid out, text labels

part.framing: a single clockwork machine part seen straight on, centered, isolated on a plain flat light gray background, game item icon, crisp edges
part.negative: background scenery, frame, border, hands, person, multiple objects

scene.framing: wide establishing shot, atmospheric depth, layered silhouettes, game background art, open calm area for interface
scene.negative: characters in the foreground, frame, border

changes: v2 (D-030): stronger ink and cel shading after the D4 review found the boss and rat airbrushed and photo-real beside Sprocket and the title
v3 (D-036): characters ask for a single figure in one pose; character sheets and turnarounds excluded (A1 tinker and Foreman came back as model sheets)
